## FastVideo FastH3 OmniRef

[FastH3 OmniRef](https://huggingface.co/FastVideo/FastH3-OmniRef-Comfy) is FastVideo's reference-to-video checkpoint on top of MiniMax H3: the distilled student (step 3500) trained with trajectory-based PDD and a joint DMD loss, so it renders synchronized video and audio in **8 sampling steps**. VSA is trained on 128-token tiles; ComfyUI runs 64-token tiles and the difference is not visible, since the larger tile only speeds up the native kernel on datacenter GPUs.

## About this workflow

This template runs the **reference-to-video (ref2va)** task with the `MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo` node. Reference images are woven into the packed sequence, so a character, a product or a location can be reused across shots while the model still generates the performance and the audio.

**Key inputs**

- **ref_images**: up to 9 reference images; two are wired here (`<Picture 1>` identity, `<Picture 2>` location). Add more slots on the node if you need them.
- **ref_videos / ref_audios**: optional, up to 3 each. A reference video can carry its own soundtrack.
- **prompt**: address the inputs by tag in connection order (`<Picture 1>`, `<Picture 2>`, …), then describe the shot, the motion and one line of dialogue; the audio follows the description.
- **ref_image_size**: `match` downscales references to the output resolution (faster), `max` keeps up to a 2048px short edge for stronger identity fidelity at the cost of speed.
- **Duration → length**: the `Float (Duration)` value is converted to the 17k+5 frame grid the model expects (5 s = 124 frames at 24fps).

## Required settings

- **Model Sparse Attention** must stay on method `vsa` with `keep_percent` 10: FastH3 checkpoints are trained with VSA and must never run plain block-sparse attention. `sol-attn` and `sla` are not compatible.
- **Model Attention Backend** only picks the dense fallback used before `start_percent` and under `min_tokens`; `comfy kitchen attention` is the int8 kernel.
- **MiniMaxH3SigmaShift** 12 / 3 is this checkpoint's video / audio shift. The FastH3 V2 text-to-video recipe (video shift 10) is not an OmniRef recipe, so do not copy it here.

## Checkpoints

Two diffusion files are published for this model: the int8 convrot export used here (22.2 GB) and a bf16 export (44.2 GB). Load exactly one of them; the text encoders and VAEs are shared with the FastH3 V2 packaging. The NVFP4 AWQ option in the text encoder folder is a text encoder, not an NVFP4 export of this diffusion model.

## Scope

This checkpoint is distilled for reference-to-video. Plain text-to-video works but is not its strength; use **FastVideo FastH3: Text to Video** or **Image to Video** for those tasks.

- [minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/vae/minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors) (577.2 MB)

- [qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/text_encoders/qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors) (14.61 GB)

📂 ComfyUI/
├── 📂 models/

subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the protagonist character whose complete identity — facial features, hairstyle, body type, skin and costume — is preserved exactly as shown in the provided character-identity reference; no visual feature of the character is changed in the target video.

summary:
[reference generation] The target video is a single continuous five-second shot in which <Subject 1>, the protagonist from the provided character-identity reference, is seen from behind in a medium close-up while the sharp focus rests on an ancient Chinese imperial palace complex in the background. The character turns sideways and then turns the head toward the camera, and as the face arrives the focus racks from the palace to the character's face, leaving the palace blurred.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the character's complete identity from the reference, including facial features, hairstyle, body type, skin and costume, is retained unchanged throughout; only the turning action and the palace background are newly generated for the target video.

detailed_description:
The target video is in a cinematic realistic style with natural daylight, shallow depth of field and a restrained, film-like color treatment. The composition is built on two visual layers: the softly blurred figure in the foreground and the sharp palace complex behind.
[Shot 1] The shot opens as a medium close-up of the upper body of <Subject 1>, the protagonist whose complete identity — facial features, hairstyle, body type, skin and costume — is preserved exactly as in the provided character-identity reference. The character stands facing away from the camera at a three-quarter back angle; only the back of the head, the shoulders and the upper back occupy the foreground, rendered softly out of focus against the daylight. The camera remains static and centered while the plane of focus rests on the background: an ancient Chinese imperial palace complex fills the frame, its layered golden roofs, vermilion walls and sweeping upturned eaves receding in ranks toward distant halls, sharp and detailed in soft daylight. The character begins to turn within the first part of the shot: the torso rotates sideways through a profile view, the weight shifts from one foot to the other, and the shoulders lead the motion; the hair and the fabric of the costume shift and settle naturally as the body moves. As the turn continues, the head rotates toward the camera and the face comes gradually into view, moving from the edge of the frame toward the center. Simultaneously the focus racks forward from the background to the character's face: the facial features sharpen into crisp clarity, gaining definition, while the palace complex falls out of focus into a soft, blurred bokeh behind, its gold and vermilion dissolving into color fields. The character finishes the turn facing the camera directly, the face occupying the central part of the frame, gaze meeting the lens, and holds the pose for a beat as the shot ends. No camera movement occurs during the shot; the only optical motion is the smooth focus pull from the background to the face.

overall_soundscape:
Quiet outdoor ambience continues throughout the video: soft wind moving across the palace grounds, faint distant birdsong and a low, distant hum of the imperial complex, all at a consistent low level.

non_diegetic_music:
N/A

widgets_values: At full `1344x768` (around 1MP) and `362` frames (15s), VSA sparse attention is about 2x faster than the int8 attention backend; at shorter, smaller clips it offers little speedup. This template uses `120 frames` (about `5s`) just to avoid OOM on some low-VRAM GPUs.
